translate_en|mods/ImmersiveSnow/42/media: Immersive Snow
Animal track lifetime (hours)
In-game hours an animal's print lasts when no snow is falling.
Animal track radius
Only animals within this many tiles of the player leave prints (the nearest 48 at most).
Animal tracks

B42 animals (deer, rabbits, chickens, cows, pigs, sheep...) and the horses, dogs and cats of the Horse Mod and Companion Dogs leave hoof and paw prints in ground snow, also out of sight, so game can be tracked. Each player can also turn them off for themselves in Options > Mods.
Barefoot prints
A player or zombie without shoes leaves the print of a bare foot (heel, ball and toes) instead of a boot sole, in the snow and with the snow carried onto clear ground.
Blood on the snow

Drops of blood behind a bleeding player or a wounded zombie, covered by snowfall like the footprints. In multiplayer only for players on this computer and zombies: the game does not tell other clients that a player bleeds. Off with the game's blood decals set to none.
Bloody steps
How many steps after the blood still leave red prints.
Bloody footprints

A player or zombie who steps on a corpse leaves red prints for the next steps, each fainter, in the snow and on clear ground (asphalt, floors). Blood on the floor alone does not count. Off with the game's blood decals set to none.
Bloody tire track length (tiles)
Tiles a wheel keeps leaving a red track after the blood, paler and paler.
Bloody tire tracks

A wheel that runs over a corpse leaves a red track that pales out: a red rut in snow, red tread marks on clear ground. Only the wheels that went over it; blood on the ground alone does not count. Follows the vanilla blood settings (none with Blood Level none or blood decals off). Each player can also turn it off for themselves in Options > Mods.
Breath vapour
Breath vapour in full (C)
Air temperature at and below which the vapour is at full strength.
Breath vapour below (C)
Air temperature at and below which the vapour shows, faint at first.
Breath vapour density
How thick the vapour is, 0.1 (barely visible) to 1.

Living players breathe out vapour in the cold: faster and thicker after running, none through a gas mask or respirator, half through cloth over the face. Uses the air temperature at the character (indoors, heaters and the vehicle heater count). Zombies do not breathe.
Snow carried on shoes and tires
Carried snow in the cold (hours)
Game hours snowy prints and tire marks on clear ground last at 0 C and below.
Carried snow melting in warmth (hours)
Game hours snowy prints and tire marks take to melt at 20 C (a heated house); at 10 C twice as long. Uses the temperature of their square.
Snowy steps off the snow
How many steps on clear ground after the snow still leave snowy prints.
Snowy tire marks off the snow (tiles)
How far a wheel leaves snowy tread marks on clear ground after the snow.
Stepping or driving from snow onto a clear square leaves a few fading snowy prints.
Snow on items in hand
Snow on what characters hold and carry on the body: weapons, tools, backpacks on the back. Off: snow on the clothes only. Turn it off if a weapon mod shows the wrong weapon models in the snow.
Snow on characters
Snow melting from body heat (hours)
Game hours body heat takes to melt a full layer of snow in the cold while it does not snow. Zombies have no body heat.
Character snow build-up (hours)
In-game hours of heavy snowfall outdoors a full layer of snow on the clothes would take (players stop at the most snow below). Light snowfall builds up slower.
Snow melting indoors above 0 C (hours)
Under a roof or in a vehicle just above 0 C a full layer of snow on a character melts in this many game hours, however cold the room; warmer rooms melt it faster still (the option above).
Most snow on a player

How much snow snowfall leaves on a player's clothes, moving about shakes off as much as falls; the lighter the snowfall, the less. 1: a full layer only in the heaviest snowfall. 1.5: a full layer in heavy snowfall, three quarters in light. Never more than a full layer. Zombies always get a full layer.
Snow melting in warmth (hours)
Game hours a full layer of snow on a character takes to melt at 20 C (indoors, by a fire, in a heated car). At 10 C it takes twice as long; below 0 C it does not melt.
Snow washed off by rain (hours)
Game hours of heavy rain above 0 C that wash a full layer of snow off a character or zombie (on top of melting in the warmth).

Snow settles on the clothes and on what you hold while you are outdoors in snowfall, and melts in warmth: indoors, by a fire, in the rain above freezing. Melting snow wets the clothes. Off: no snow on characters at all, so none melts into the clothes (falling snow and walking through snow still wet them).
No corpse flies or stench in frost

While it is 0 C or colder outdoors, no flies buzz over corpses and their stench makes nobody sick: the mod holds the game's "Decaying Corpse Health Impact" at None and sets it back above +1 C. If you set that option yourself while it is held, the mod leaves it as you set it and turns this option off. Before taking the mod out of a save, run ISnow.cleanSave() in the console (see the mod page), or that option may stay at None.
Snow stays on corpses

A zombie or player that dies with snow on keeps it on the corpse, and it melts there as on zombies: in warmth above freezing, in the rain, and within an hour once the ground outdoors is bare. No new snow settles on corpses. Off: the snow comes off when a character dies. In multiplayer only on the corpses of deaths this client saw.
Darker snow
Darker snow on vehicles, characters and items, and darker snow particles, to match darker ground snow. On by itself with Snow Lands - Darker Snow. Takes effect after loading the save again.
Drifting snow
Drifting snow: amount
How much snow dust drifts: 1 is about 30 wisps a second on the screen at full wind, 2 twice as many.
Drifting snow: from wind speed (km/h)
Wind speed from which snow drifts along the ground; it grows to full 30 km/h above it.
In a strong wind in the frost, low snow dust sweeps along the ground snow with the wind, in gusts. In multiplayer each player can hide it for themselves in Options > Mods.
Snow thaws around fires
Snow thaws around fires: patch lasts (hours)
Game hours a fully thawed patch takes to go after the fire is out, if no snow falls (falling snow covers it faster).

A campfire, a fire on the ground or a burning building melts the snow around it into a dark wet patch, with a little steam, while it burns. The patch freezes over and is snowed over after the fire goes out. In multiplayer each player can hide it for themselves in Options > Mods.
Footprint lifetime (hours)
In-game hours a player's footprint lasts when no snow is falling.
Footprints left by
Everyone (players and zombies)
Players only
Nobody (off)

Who leaves footprints in ground snow: everyone (players and the zombies near a player), players only, or nobody (no footprints and no snow carried off on the soles). Each player can also show fewer for themselves in Options > Mods.
Frost on the screen in hypothermia
Frost on the screen: creeps in (seconds)
Real seconds the frost takes to creep in to the next stage when the Hypothermia moodle rises. In multiplayer always as on the server.
Frost on the screen: from Hypothermia level
Level of the Hypothermia moodle (1-4) at which the first frost shows at the edges of the screen. It reaches further in at each level above, in full at level 4. In multiplayer always as on the server.
Frost on the screen: thaws (seconds)
Real seconds the frost takes to thaw back when the Hypothermia moodle drops or goes. In multiplayer always as on the server.
Frost on the screen: opacity
How thick the frost at the edges of the screen is at its fullest, 0.1 (barely visible) to 1. In multiplayer always as on the server.
Frost on the screen trembles
Frost on the screen trembles: from Hypothermia level
Level of the Hypothermia moodle (1-4) at which the frost starts to tremble.
The frost at the edges of the screen trembles while the character shivers with cold, harder at each Hypothermia level. Turn off if screen motion bothers you.

Frost creeps in from the edges of the screen with the Hypothermia moodle: further in at each level, in full at level 4. Goes away as the character warms up. In multiplayer each player can hide it for themselves in Options > Mods.
Special mode for @melixrism (Low-end graphics)

For weak integrated graphics with little video memory. Turns off snow on zombies, on items in hand and on vehicle doors, hoods and wheels, and the icing on vehicles; fewer footprints and tire tracks (at most 600 / 1200), zombie footprints only within 15 tiles, fewer snow particles blown off cars, half the footprint textures. The same switch is in Options > Mods for each player.
Max animal prints
Above this limit the oldest animal prints fade out (a limit of their own, apart from the footprints). Lower it if the game slows down by a farm in snow.
Max footprints
Above this limit the oldest footprints fade out. Players and zombies share it (each keeps at least half); lower it if the game slows down in snow.
Max tire track segments
A segment is 0.4 tile of one wheel's track. Hard limit: above it the oldest segments vanish within seconds; lower it if the game slows down in snow.
Snow washed away by rain (hours)

Game hours of rain that wash a full cover of snow off the ground, in stages: the snow thins out, the prints and the depth go with it; heavy rain is twice as fast. 0: all at once at the next hour, as in vanilla. In MP the server decides.
3D snow on the ground

Only in the 3D view of Viewpoint with the Immersive Snow - Viewpoint add-on: the snow on the ground has a depth (prints, ruts and furrows pressed into it). Off: the ground snow is flat, as Viewpoint lays it.
3D snow on vehicles

Only in the 3D view of Viewpoint with the Immersive Snow - Viewpoint add-on: the snow on vehicles lies on top as a layer with a thickness (roof, bonnet, boot). Off: the snow on vehicles is flat, as in the isometric view.
Snow depth (cm)

Only with the Immersive Snow - Viewpoint add-on: depth of the snow on the ground in Viewpoint's 3D view at the highest snow level, less while it is building up or melting. The snow also drifts deeper against buildings, steps run together into a trench and shovelled squares stand as cuttings; from 10 cm it slows you down (3D snow slows you down).
Snow kicked up
Snow kicked up: size of the puff from a fall
How much snow a fall raises: 1 is 7 puffs and 3 clumps, 2 twice as many.
Snow kicked up: falls
A player or zombie that goes down in the snow (knocked down, tripped, killed) raises a puff along the body.
Snow kicked up: running
Powder puffs a running step into snow throws (a fraction is the chance of one): 0 none, 0.4 about every other step, 3 a lot.
Snow kicked up: sprinting
Powder puffs a sprinting step into snow throws, with a chance of a clump.
Snow thrown up by wheels: amount
How much snow the wheels throw: 1 is about 40 puffs a second off a car at 40 km/h and over, 2 twice as many.
Snow thrown up by wheels
Vehicle wheels in snow throw powder and now and then a clump behind them: more the faster the vehicle goes, more again when it slides sideways. Works with tire tracks off too.
Running and sprinting through snow throws a little powder back off the feet; a player or zombie that goes down in the snow (knocked down, tripped, killed) raises a puff. Only with footprints on.
3D snow slows you down

Only with the Immersive Snow - Viewpoint add-on (its 3D snow on the ground): from 10 cm of snow (Snow depth) wading through it tires you, from 30 cm you cannot sprint, and a vehicle you drive goes slower (at 45 cm about half its top speed). Not on squares cleared with a shovel; on trampled paths it is easier. In MP the server decides.
Snow thickness on vehicles in 3D (%%)

Only in the 3D view of Viewpoint with the Immersive Snow - Viewpoint add-on: the snow on vehicles stands out as a layer where it settles on top (the roof, the bonnet: up to about 12 cm at the last stage at 100%%); clothes, the vehicles' sides, ice and frost on the glass stay flat. 0: flat, as before.
Snow wets clothes
Snow wetting rate
Multiplier of how fast snow wets the clothes. 1 = wet snow at 0 C soaks an outer layer in about 3 game hours; the colder, the drier the snow.

Snow falling on a player and the snow melting on the clothes make them wet, like rain does in vanilla; walking through snow wets the shoes. Water-resistant clothes and boots protect. Wet clothes keep less warm.
Snowfall cover speed
How much faster footprints disappear during heavy snowfall.
Tire track lifetime (hours)
In-game hours a tire track lasts when no snow is falling.
Tire track segments before old ones fade
Above this many segments the oldest fade out over about 20 seconds, so a spot driven over again and again keeps only its latest laps. Has no effect at or above the max segments.
Tire tracks
Vehicles leave tire tracks in ground snow. Off: no tire tracks and no snow carried off on the tires. Each player can also turn them off for themselves in Options > Mods.
Trampled paths: last (hours)
Game hours a path lasts after the last walker, if no snow falls (falling snow covers it faster).
Trampled paths: footprints to make one
Footprints on one square that make a path there (older ones count less, half after 3 game hours); the path gets darker with more. About 2 footprints a square each time someone walks through.
Trampled paths

Snow walked over again and again (players and zombies) becomes a trodden path that lasts much longer than footprints: you can see where a horde keeps walking. Counted from the footprints, so only with footprints on. In multiplayer each player can hide them for themselves in Options > Mods.
Frost on vehicle windows
Frost on vehicle windows: heater thaw (minutes)
Game minutes the heater (with the engine running) takes to clear fully frosted windows. The engine alone takes four times as long. In multiplayer always as on the server.
Frost on vehicle windows: hours to full
Game hours a vehicle parked outdoors at -8 C or colder takes to frost over fully. Slower in a milder frost, none above 0 C. In multiplayer always as on the server.
Frost on vehicle windows: thaw in the warm (hours)
Game hours full frost takes to thaw on its own at +5 C; at +10 C half as long. Below 0 C it does not thaw on its own. In multiplayer always as on the server.

A vehicle parked outdoors in the frost gets frost on its windows, on the glass itself. Scrape it off (right-click the vehicle; faster with a scraper, spatula or trowel) or run the engine with the heater on. In multiplayer each player can hide it for themselves in Options > Mods.
Hood melts from the engine
Hood melts from the engine: hours
Game hours a hot engine takes to melt a full layer of snow off the hood. A cold engine melts nothing; half warm, twice as long. In multiplayer always as on the server.

While the engine is warm, the snow on the hood melts faster than on the roof: the hotter the engine, the faster (vanilla engine temperature: it warms up over the first hour or so of running and stays warm for a while after it stops). Only on vehicles whose hood is a separate model (KI5, Vanilla Vehicles Animated...); on the vanilla cars the hood is part of the body. In multiplayer the server decides; each player can hide it for themselves in Options > Mods.
Snow on vehicles
Vehicle snow build-up (hours)
In-game hours of heavy snowfall until a parked vehicle is fully covered.
Icing on vehicles
Glazed ice around the snow on the body, the wheels and the glass edges. Off: plain snow only. Frost on the glass is a separate option.
Snow builds up on vehicles parked outdoors, melts in warmth and from a running engine, and blows off when driving. Works with modded vehicles.
Zombie footprint lifetime (hours)
In-game hours a zombie's footprint lasts when no snow is falling. Lower it so hordes do not trample the snow for long.
Zombie footprint radius
Only zombies within this many tiles of the player leave footprints.
Snow on zombies
Snow build-up on zombies (hours)
Game hours of heavy snowfall until a zombie outdoors is fully covered. Melting works as for players, without body heat; outdoors on bare ground the snow goes within an hour.
Zombies get snow on their clothes too. They have no body heat: the snow melts in warmth above freezing or in the rain, and goes within an hour once the ground outdoors is bare.

Off: no red footprints after stepping on a corpse for you, whatever the sandbox says. On: as the sandbox says, in single player with "Use these settings instead of the sandbox" on. Also off with the vanilla blood decals off.

Off: no red tire tracks after running over a corpse for you, whatever the sandbox says. On: as the sandbox says, in single player with "Use these settings instead of the sandbox" on. Also off with the vanilla blood decals off.
Sound of snow flying off vehicles
A soft thump and hiss when a layer of snow flies off a vehicle going fast. Heard only by you; zombies do not hear it.
Brush the snow off (by hand)
Brush the snow off (%1)
Clear the snow (%1)
Clear the snow around (%1)
Detailed tracks and footprints
Three shapes of every footprint and tire track segment, so trails do not repeat. Off: one shape, a third of the video memory for their textures.

Whose footprints you see: everyone's, players' only or nobody's (no footprints, no snow off the soles). The lesser of this and the sandbox counts; in single player with "Use these settings instead of the sandbox" this alone. In multiplayer never more than the server has.

Off: no frost creeping in from the edges of your screen in hypothermia, whatever the sandbox says. On: as the sandbox says, in single player with "Use these settings instead of the sandbox" on. In multiplayer you can hide it for yourself; how thick and from which level are the server's.
Special mode for @melixrism (Low-end graphics)
For weak integrated graphics: no snow on zombies, items and vehicle doors and wheels, no vehicle icing, fewer footprints and tire tracks. Also turned on by the same sandbox option.

The same settings as on the sandbox page, but only on your computer. What you turn off here stays hidden for you even with the box below cleared. In multiplayer only the on/off switches work (to hide for yourself what the server has on), every number follows the server.
Your settings
Scrape frost off the windows (by hand)
Scrape frost off the windows (%1)
Shake the snow off

Off: the ground snow in Viewpoint's 3D view is flat for you, whatever the sandbox says. With the 3D snow on vehicles off too, there is no 3D snow anywhere. Only with the Immersive Snow - Viewpoint add-on.

Off: the snow on vehicles in Viewpoint's 3D view is flat for you (no snow caps on top), whatever the sandbox says. With the 3D snow on the ground off too, there is no 3D snow anywhere. Only with the Immersive Snow - Viewpoint add-on.
Off: the 3D snow does not slow you down. In multiplayer the server alone decides, this switch does nothing there. Only with the Immersive Snow - Viewpoint add-on.

Off: no tire tracks and no snow off the tires for you, whatever the sandbox says. Try this first if the game stutters while driving. On: as the sandbox says, in single player with "Use these settings instead of the sandbox" on.
Immersive Snow
Use these settings instead of the sandbox

Single player only. On: the settings below replace the sandbox settings of the save, also in an existing save. Off: the sandbox decides, but what you turn off below stays hidden for you. In multiplayer this box does nothing: what you turn off below is hidden for you, everything else (durations, limits, rates) follows the server; wetness from snow follows the server entirely and cannot be turned off.

Off: no frost on vehicle windows for you (nothing to scrape, a clear view from inside), whatever the sandbox says. On: as the sandbox says, in single player with "Use these settings instead of the sandbox" on. In multiplayer you can hide it for yourself; how fast it grows and thaws is the server's.

Off: no faster melting on the hood of a warm engine for you, whatever the sandbox says; the hood keeps the snow of the rest of the body. On: as the sandbox says, in single player with "Use these settings instead of the sandbox" on. Only on vehicles whose hood is a separate model (KI5, Vanilla Vehicles Animated...). In multiplayer you can hide it for yourself; whether it melts and how fast is the server's.
